trigger: gateway or watcher restart inside nextUpdate+grace while a stale but validly signed CRL is served
classification_rationale: a statement, test or behaviour that the code does not support or that contradicts another published statement
summary: Replay protection is in memory only: a restart starts from crl=none and accepts any validly signed CRL, so a stale CRL served at restart can re-admit a withdrawn server certificate for up to nextUpdate+grace. Also raised independently by gateway-erlang (ge-F2), architect and quality-engineer (probe reproduced it). Derived HIGH via I1/E5; native label MEDIUM disagrees, derived governs.

Owner decision 2026-11-04 (ADR 2004 A8): the watcher's tick state is seeded from the published CRL (seeded_state/0, source.erl init/1), pinned by restart_keeps_the_high_water_mark_test. Fixes the WATCHER restart only; the whole-gateway residual is sec-F1b.

trigger: gateway process starts afresh and the CRL source serves an older, still-valid CRL
classification_rationale: a statement, test or behaviour that the code does not support or that contradicts another published statement
summary: A restart of the whole gateway empties persistent_term and so forgets the high-water mark; the first validly signed CRL it is given is accepted, however old, for at most that CRL's nextUpdate+grace (about 3 days at 48 h validity, about 8 against a 7-day-CRL server). Needs a restored server database or a holder of a certificate for the server's HTTPS name to serve the older CRL. Whether E2 applies (a revoked-credential holder regaining command authority) is unresolved.
